recipes.name: Ginny’s Mini Cheesecakes
ingredients_raw: 1 (21 ounce) can cherry pie filling, or flavor of choice

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Line muffin tins with 12 paper baking cups. Place a vanilla wafer in each one.
In a medium mixing bowl beat cream cheese until fluffy. Add eggs, lemon juice, and sugar. Beat until smooth and thoroughly combined.
Fill each baking cup 2/3 full with cream cheese mixture.
Bake in preheated oven for 15 to 17 minutes. Cool on a rack. Top with fruit pie filling or topping of your choice.

raw_recipe.headline: Ginny’s Mini Cheesecakes
raw_recipe.description: Muffin tins are lined with paper baking cups and a vanilla wafer “crust,” then filled with a lemony cheesecake batter and baked. Top with your favorite fruit pie filling, if desired.

review.reviewBody: These are wonderful! I tried this. Melt some Kraft caramels, put about 1 tsp caramel and 1/2 tsp chpped pecans on top of nilla wafer before adding cheesecake mixture bake as usual, just before completely cool, top with a little melted milk chocolate chips, drizzle with a little more caramel and sprinkle few more pecans. OH MY GOSH YUMMY!

I made this recipe 2x, for different events. The first time, I followed it exactly. I found that I didn't like the addition of the lemon juice and missed the graham cracker crust. I also found they cooked too quickly and cracked or turned brown. People liked it, but they didn't seem to love it. The second time, I made a graham cracker crust using 6 sheets of graham crackers (I used store brand), 1/3 C brown sugar, and 6 T melted butter. I stirred it together and put 1 heaping tsp into each paper cup. Then, using a round spice container pushed the graham into the little cups. For the cheesecake filling, I subbed the lemon with about 2 tsp vanilla and added 1T of milk, to thin it out a bit. I lowered the temp to 325, and baked 14 mins. Out of 42 cheesecakes, 2 cracked and none browned. Some of them I topped with cherry pie filling; some I topped with fresh chopped strawberries; and the rest I topped with the remainder of the graham cracker crumb mixture and a drizzle of chocolate syrup. All loved it. And, I did not have 1 left over. This is a great recipe that you can definitely make your own.

Love this recipe! Once, I made the mistake of buying mini vanilla wafers, so here’s what I did:

1. Pulse 1/2 a box vanilla wafers in food processor until it’s crumbs.
2. Melt 1/2 stick butter (1/4 cup) in microwave and pour into crumbs and mix. 
3. Drop 1 small scoop of crust mixture in each cupcake paper. 
4. Press into bottom with a spice jar. 
5. Make cheesecake batter as recipe says. 
6. Drop 1 large scoop cheesecake batter into each cupcake paper. 
7. Bake 20 minutes at 350 degrees. 
8. Recipe yields about 16-17 cupcakes.

Turned out great! The boyfriend loved them for our anniversary~! I substituted the nilla wafers with 1/3 cup crushed graham cracker mixed with 1/4 tbs butter for the base. Then I hand pressed them into the cupcake paper wrappers and poured the cheesecake batter over top to the 2/3rds mark. Tasted delicious and topped it with my own strawberry syrup and a dollop of whipped cream. Yummy yummy!!!

Everyone who has tasted these has absolutely flipped for them. These are so delicious and best of all, exceedingly easy to make. I baked them for 18-20 minutes making them much less likely to drop in the center. Topped with fresh fruit instead of a filling. Amazing. You can also try using 1 container of strawberry cream cheese and one original. Reduce sugar to 1/2 cup. Top with fresh strawberries or chocolate chips.

I really like this recipe. To remove the sugar entirely, I decided not to use a cookie or any graham crackers for the bottom. Instead of the 2/3 cup of sugar, I used 2/3 cup of NuNaturals MoreFiber Baking Blend (Stevia). I followed the advice of other reviewers and made them in cupcake liners, cooled them, and froze them. The cupcake paper comes off nicely when they are frozen. These modifications resulted in the healthiest cheesecake dessert I've ever made or eaten. I would make it again this way. In the words of a previous reviewer, this is such a versatile recipe. I'm grateful that the original cook shared it!

These were a huge hit! Easy to make and everyone loved them. I dropped an Oreo in as my crust, reduced the lemon and added alittle more vanilla. Once they have cooled do not put your toppings on, refrigerate overnight and next day the liners come right off. put toppings on and serve. Side note: if the tops crack you over baked them.

These are awesome!! I prefer graham cracker crust so I used the graham cracker, butter, sugar mix for the bottoms. I also made mine in ramekins instead of a cupcake pan. I halved the recipe and it made 4 ramekin desserts. Otherwise, made it exactly as stated. Turned out great! Not overly sweet like cheesecake can be. Also, the texture was great for me, not mushy.
 I've made cheesecake before with vanilla wafers and even with animal crackers if I don't have graham crackers and both work just fine. Just for my personal taste, I like the graham cracker crust.
 I had cherry pie filling to top them with and caramel with pecans. Tried them both ways and I prefer the caramel topping or just plain because the cherry pie filling seemed to overpower the taste of the cheesecake. And this is definitely a cheesecake you want to savor in your mouth!

This recipe is awesome! I only changed 2 things. I don't like using lemon juice in my cheesecakes so I used a tablespoon of vanilla instead. I didn't have the vanilla wafers so I made a graham cracker crust. Which is personally my favorite with cheesecake. Other than that these mini cheesecakes came out so smooth and oh so yummy. I also think of prefer the mini cheesecakes to making a regular cheesecake because it is portion controlled LOL

Yummy and easy to make. I made a pretzel crust mixture (butter, brown sugar and pretzel pieces) that I put into the bottom of foil cupcake liners ( which hold their shape well). Made the recipe for the cheesecake as written. Of course my kiddos and I ate some as soon as we thought they were cool enough :0) I made my crust a little bit thicker..and enjoyed eating them plain and topped some with a sour cream and sugar topping (mix to your taste). Left them in the fridge for a couple hours to chill. Everyone loved them. Making more today!!

Made these with my girlfriend, they turned out absolutely lovely. We realized quickly that the wafer cookies weren't exactly suiting our needs, so we put some graham crackers, butter, and brown sugar in a food processor and baked for a while in order to make a more traditional crust. Using these, we had great results. They needed a little bit of extra time in the oven, and the texture improved drastically after refrigerating for a few hours. Aside from those few notes, they were wonderful. We ended up with quite a bit of extra and made several extra cheesecakes, which was a pleasant surprise. Will absolutely come back to this recipe at some point.

These were easy and great! I added cut up vanilla wafers to accommodate the extra space in cupcake paper——-easier than graham cracker crust / no complaints from grandkids! Squited reddi- whip and put Anerican flag pics for 4th of July- big hit!
This is my go to recipe for a quick delicious dessert. Everyone loves them!
Made this recipe many times. Simple, quick and a definite crowd pleaser.
Delicious! It's my go-to when I want cheesecake and don't want to spend $7 a slice.

I have been using this for over 10 years! I have switched up the crust from gluten free to Oreo to teddy grahams. I get compliments all the time. I usually forgo the lemon juice and add vanilla extract. I have done a few flavours but my biggest hit is my pumpkin cheesecake. Thank you sooo much for sharing!!
My vanilla wafers didn't fully cover the bottom, but don't worry. These turn out great and are easy to make!
Perfection but I couldn’t find vanilla wafers so I went with a graham crumb base. Worked

I have been looking for THIS recipe for YEARS!! This is a dessert my grandmother used to make for our family 4th of July parties. She used blueberry and cherry pie filling on top and left some plan and put them into a flag like pattern on the buffet tables.. I remember being a little kid and just LOVING these. The way they looked with silver liners and the way she presented it and of course they tasted AMAZING and created my life long love of cheesecakes! But since she has passed no one had any idea of the recand I've been looking for YEARS and FINALLY found this!!! This is the EXACT recipe, lol once my mother saw it she had a memory cluck especially since these are SO EASY to make and have only a few ingredients. In our families opinion these are better than regular full size cheesecakes.. The only problem we ever have is there are never enough and everyone wants more! The only changes I made is I use a 1/2 cup of sugar because we prefer a less sweet cheesecake when adding the pie filling to the tops. Also for anyone that sees this know you CAN always add more or less sugar depending on your personal tastes. My friend makes her with a whole cup of sugar! For me that was far to sweet, but everyone has their preferred way! But these are ALWAYS a hit if you have cheesecake lovers!

An awesome dessert option. I didn't use the vanilla wafer, it appeared to small to cover the bottom of the muffin pan. Instead I substituted crushed graham cracker with melted butter for the crust. I doubled the recipe, but there is no need to double the cherry topping; 1 can is plenty. Also, I found that to only fill the muffin tin 2/3 full made for skimpy (cookie height) minis. Next time I will fill to the top of the liner for better presentation. I did bake in a water bath and had no cracking. Update 2022: I made 1.5 of the recipe, filled the cupcake tins 3/4, and baked exactly 20 minutes~this did the trick!Note: use room temp cream cheese and overnight chill for best flavor as with any cheesecake it brings out the sweetness
